title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378D (Membership and voting rights of Members of Producer Company)

content.overview: Voting rights in a Producer Company depend on membership composition: single vote per Member where membership is solely individual or mixed; participation-based (or shareholding in the first year) where membership consists only of Producer Institutions. Articles may set retention conditions and restrict voting to active Members. Conflict-of-interest persons cannot become or remain Members.
content.glance: One-member-one-vote for individuals/mixed; participation-based for Producer Institutions only; conflict-of-interest bar.
content.study: Section 378D(1) fixes voting rights according to the composition of membership. Articles may provide conditions for continued membership and the manner of exercise of voting rights, and may restrict voting to active Members. No person with a business interest conflicting with the Producer Company may become a Member; a Member who acquires such an interest ceases to be a Member and is removed in accordance with the articles.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Voting rights are single-vote for individual or mixed membership and participation-based for Producer Institutions only; conflict-of-interest bars membership.

provisions.title: Membership and voting rights of Members of Producer Company

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378D
examples.body: In an individual-only Producer Company each Member has one vote irrespective of shareholding or patronage.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378D?
hypotheticals.analysis: It determines voting rights by membership composition and excludes persons with conflicting business interests.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming shareholding always determines voting power.
misconceptions.correction: For individual or mixed membership, voting is one Member one vote; shareholding is irrelevant.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify membership composition. II. Apply the corresponding voting rule and conflict bar. III. Conclude.
